dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:6101.text: A kind of 貍 beast. Formed from 豸, with 苗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6102.text: Like a wild ox, but blue-green. Pictographic; its head is the same as in 禽 and 离. All characters in this group are formed from 𤉡.

shuowen:6103.text: The lizard, 蜥易 or 蝘蜓, also called 守宮. Pictographic. The Secret Writings explains: 日 and 月 make 易, representing yin and yang. Another explanation: it follows 勿. All characters in this group are formed from 易.

shuowen:6104.text: A great beast of Southern Yue with a long trunk and tusks, bearing young once in three years. Depicts ears, tusks and four feet. All characters in this group are formed from 象.

shuowen:6105.text: A large elephant. Palace Attendant Jia explains: not harming other things. Formed from 象, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6106.text: Anger; martial strength. Depicts a horse’s head, mane, tail and four feet. All characters in this group are formed from 馬.

shuowen:6107.text: A stallion. Formed from 馬, with 陟 indicating the sound. Read like 郅.

shuowen:6108.text: A one-year-old horse. Formed from 馬, with 一 hobbling its feet. Read like 弦, or alternatively like 環.

shuowen:6109.text: A two-year-old horse is 駒; a three-year-old, 駣. Formed from 馬, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6110.text: An eight-year-old horse. Formed from 馬 and 八.

shuowen:6111.text: A horse with one white eye is 𩦂; with two white eyes, 魚. Formed from 馬, with 閒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6112.text: A blue-black horse with markings like a gaming board. Formed from 馬, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6113.text: A deep-black horse. Formed from 馬, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6114.text: A blue-black horse. Formed from 馬, with 肙 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Well fed are that team of blue-black horses.”

shuowen:6115.text: A light-black horse. Formed from 馬, with 鬼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6116.text: A red horse with black mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 畱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6117.text: A horse with mixed red and white hair. Formed from 馬, with 叚 indicating the sound, referring to a color resembling shrimp.

shuowen:6118.text: A horse with mixed blue-gray and black hair. Formed from 馬, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6119.text: A white horse with black mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6120.text: A horse with mixed dark and white hair: black. Formed from 馬, with 因 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “There are 駰 and 騢 horses.”

shuowen:6121.text: A horse with mixed blue-gray and white hair. Formed from 馬, with 悤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6122.text: A black horse with white flanks. Formed from 馬, with 矞 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “There are 驈 and 騜 horses.”

shuowen:6123.text: A horse with face and forehead both white. Formed from 馬, with 尨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6124.text: A yellow horse with a black muzzle. Formed from 馬, with 咼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6125.text: A yellow horse showing white. Another explanation: with white mane and tail. Formed from 馬, with 𤐫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6126.text: A yellow horse with white hair. Formed from 馬, with 丕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6127.text: A red-black horse. Formed from 馬, with 𢧜 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Four red-black horses, very large.”

shuowen:6128.text: A horse with red hair on its head. Formed from 馬, with 岸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6129.text: A horse with a white forehead. Formed from 馬, with abbreviated 的 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a fine horse. The Changes says: “It is a white-marked forehead.”

shuowen:6130.text: A horse of mixed color. Formed from 馬, with 爻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6131.text: A horse with a white left hind foot. Formed from 馬, with 二 marking its feet. Read like 注.

shuowen:6132.text: A black horse with a yellow back. Formed from 馬, with 覃 indicating the sound. Read like 簟.

shuowen:6133.text: A horse with a white rear, written 州 in the recorded gloss; that wording is uncertain. Formed from 馬, with 燕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6134.text: A horse with hairy shins. Formed from 馬, with 習 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6135.text: A horse with long hair. Formed from 馬, with 倝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6136.text: A horse swift of foot. Formed from 馬 and 飛. The Methods of the Minister of War says: “Swiftly guard this chariot.”

shuowen:6137.text: A fine horse. It dies on a renshen day; riders avoid this taboo. Formed from 馬, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6138.text: A thousand-li horse, of the kind Sun Yang judged. Formed from 馬, with 冀 indicating the sound. Tianshui has Ji County, 驥.

shuowen:6139.text: A horse of excellent ability. Formed from 馬, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6140.text: A good horse. Formed from 馬, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6141.text: The appearance of a small horse. Formed from 馬, with 垂 indicating the sound. Read like 箠.

shuowen:6142.text: A horse six chi high is 驕. Formed from 馬, with 喬 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “My horses are tall.” Another explanation: a wild horse.

shuowen:6143.text: A horse seven chi high is 騋; eight chi, 龍. Formed from 馬, with 來 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Tall mares and black stallions.”

shuowen:6144.text: A horse’s name. Formed from 馬, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6145.text: A horse’s name. Formed from 馬, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6146.text: A horse’s name. Formed from 馬, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6147.text: A horse’s name. Formed from 馬, with 休 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6148.text: A horse with a red mane, white body and eyes like gold is called 𩢌. Jihuang’s mount; in King Wen of Zhou’s time, the Quanrong presented it. Formed from 馬 and 文; 文 also indicates the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “A hundred teams of 𩢌 horses,” meaning patterned horses. The Earl of the West presented them to King Zhou of Shang (紂) to preserve himself.

shuowen:6149.text: A strong horse. Formed from 馬, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6150.text: A well-fed horse. Formed from 馬, with 必 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Well fed, well fed.”

shuowen:6151.text: A flourishing, fat horse. Formed from 馬, with 光 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The four stallions are fat and strong.”

shuowen:6152.text: Horses flourishing. Formed from 馬, with 㫄 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The four stallions are vigorous.”

shuowen:6153.text: 䭹䭹, a horse’s angry appearance. Formed from 馬, with 卬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6154.text: A horse lowering and raising its head. Formed from 馬, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6155.text: To mount a horse. Formed from 馬, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6156.text: To straddle a horse. Formed from 馬, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6157.text: A horse within the yoke. Formed from 馬, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6158.text: An outrunner, a horse at the side. Formed from 馬, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6159.text: To harness two horses. Formed from 馬, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6160.text: To harness three horses. Formed from 馬, with 參 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6161.text: A team of horses. Formed from 馬, with 四 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6162.text: A reserve horse. Formed from 馬, with 付 indicating the sound. Another explanation: near. Another: swift.

shuowen:6163.text: A horse compliant or harmonious. Formed from 馬, with 皆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6164.text: A horse shaking its head. Formed from 馬, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6165.text: Head-shaking, 駊騀. Formed from 馬, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6166.text: A horse’s manner of moving. Formed from 馬, with 舀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6167.text: A horse moving slowly and haltingly. Formed from 馬, with 竹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6168.text: A horse moving with dignified bearing. Formed from 馬, with 癸 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The four stallions move majestically.”

shuowen:6169.text: A horse moving slowly yet swiftly. Formed from 馬, with abbreviated 學 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6170.text: A horse moving swiftly. Formed from 馬, with abbreviated 㑴 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Then galloping, swiftly onward.”

shuowen:6171.text: Horses catching up with one another. Formed from 馬 and 及. The reading is referred to the Erya’s “Small mountains: 馺; large mountains: 峘.”

shuowen:6172.text: A horse moving swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 冫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6173.text: A horse stepping swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 耴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6174.text: A horse moving vigorously, 㐹㐹. Formed from 馬, with 矣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6175.text: A horse’s rapid steps. Formed from 馬, with 聚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6176.text: A horse running swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 匃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6177.text: A horse’s rapid steps. Formed from 馬, with 風 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6178.text: A horse galloping. Formed from 馬, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6179.text: A great gallop. Formed from 馬, with 也 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6180.text: To gallop in disorder. Formed from 馬, with 敄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6181.text: To gallop in successive order. Formed from 馬, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6182.text: To gallop straight ahead. Formed from 馬, with 甹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6183.text: A horse coming swiftly. Formed from 馬, with 兌 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The Kunyi sped away.”

shuowen:6184.text: A horse with swift feet. Formed from 馬, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6185.text: A horse charging suddenly. Formed from 馬, with 旱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6186.text: To gallop a horse straight away. Formed from 馬, with 同 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6187.text: A horse frightened. Formed from 馬, with 敬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6188.text: Frightened. Formed from 馬, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6189.text: A horse bolting. Formed from 馬, with 巟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6190.text: A horse’s belly bound or constricted. Formed from 馬, with abbreviated 寒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6191.text: A horse standing still. Formed from 馬, with 主 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6192.text: A horse obedient. Formed from 馬, with 川 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6193.text: A horse having difficulty bearing a heavy load. Formed from 馬, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6194.text: Laboring under a load, 駗驙. Formed from 馬, with 亶 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “The team of horses strains onward.”

shuowen:6195.text: A horse’s burdened appearance. Formed from 馬, with 執 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6196.text: A horse with a curved back. Formed from 馬, with 鞠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6197.text: A castrated horse. Formed from 馬, with 乘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6198.text: To tie a horse’s tail. Formed from 馬, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6199.text: To disturb. Another explanation: to rub a horse. Formed from 馬, with 蚤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:6200.text: To hobble a horse. Formed from 馬, enclosing its feet with 囗. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Han Jue held the hobbles and went forward.” Read like 輒.
